newsitem.title: USA: Mass auditor seen rejecting bus privatizing--paper.
newsitem.headline: Mass auditor seen rejecting bus privatizing--paper.

text.p: A Massachusetts state offical likely will reject private contracts to run about 40 percent of the MBTA bus routes, the state transportation secretary predicted, the Boston Globe reported Friday.

Transportation secretary James Kerasiotes said he expected auditor Joseph DeNucci to turn down the contracts for the largest privatization deal to date. The five-year bids exceed $305 million, and the MBTA says they will save about $27 milion over five years, the Globe said, adding Kerasiotes might challenge in court a rejection by the auditor.

The paper said DeNucci refused to tip his hand, but said sources were saying his staff had serious doubts about the estimated savings. DeNucci has the power to reject contracts if he finds they will fail to save money or at least ensure adequate service.
DeNucci, a Democrat, and Kerasiotes, a Republican, both are considering running next year for state treasurer, the paper said.
It added labor unions oppose such privatization efforts.
